run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Social Network
Namespace: social-network

A social network with unidirectional follow relationships, implemented with loosely-coupled microservices, communicating with each other via Thrift RPCs.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The social-network application itself (27 helm-installed Deployments: nginx-thrift, compose-post-service, text-service, home-timeline-service, user-timeline-service, social-graph-service, post-storage-service, user-service, user-mention-service, url-shorten-service, media-service, unique-id-service and their mongo/redis/memcached backends) came up at 2026-11-24T04:16:04Z with all replicas Ready and 0 restarts, has populated endpoints for all 26 Services, and the sampled traces of the frontend in 04:16:16-04:16:29 show only HTTP 200 spans with sub-10 ms durations. The one clearly broken workload is a separate Deployment, custom-service (namespace social-network), which was created by kubectl-client-side-apply at 04:16:11Z from a plain python:3.9-slim http.server manifest and then mutated at 04:16:13Z by a kubectl-patch to add an init container hang-init (busybox:1.36, /bin/sh -c 'sleep infinity'). With strategy maxSurge 0%/maxUnavailable 100%, the previously working ReplicaSet was scaled to 0 while the new pods can never finish their init container: all 3 custom-service pods stay in phase Pending with Init=False (ContainersNotInitialized), main container waiting PodInitializing, and the Deployment reports 3 replicas / 3 unavailable. Grafana/Prometheus history for the authorized window is effectively absent (Prometheus returns a single sample at 04:16:30Z), so error-rate/latency trends before that instant are unknown, and no user-visible impact of the custom-service outage could be observed (it has no Service or Ingress and no observed callers).

claims.text: Deployment custom-service in namespace social-network carries init container hang-init with image busybox:1.36 and command /bin/sh -c "sleep infinity" in its pod template, with replicas 3 and rollingUpdate maxSurge 0% / maxUnavailable 100%.

custom-service was created at 2026-11-24T04:16:11Z by manager kubectl-client-side-apply (generation 1, last-applied-configuration without any init container) and then updated at 2026-11-24T04:16:13Z by managers kubectl-patch and kubectl-rollout, reaching generation 3; its status now shows replicas 3, updatedReplicas 3, unavailableReplicas 3.

The three pods custom-service-9cf9bfd98-2pdgp, -bxsrs and -k8ctv are in phase Pending: their init container hang-init is running (startedAt 2026-11-24T04:16:14Z), the Initialized condition is False with reason ContainersNotInitialized ("containers with incomplete status: [hang-init]"), and the main container custom-service-main is not started (waiting reason PodInitializing, ready false, restartCount 0).

Events for the same rollout show Deployment custom-service scaling replica set custom-service-9cf9bfd98 from 0 to 3 and replica set custom-service-5c68f797 from 3 to 0 at 2026-11-24T04:16:13Z, and containers named hang-init Started on the new pods (container image busybox:1.36) at 04:16:14Z.

All three custom-service pods were successfully scheduled (Scheduled events, assigned to sregym-worker/worker2/worker3), so the Pending phase is caused by the never-ending init container and not by unschedulability; there are no FailedScheduling events for them and no ResourceQuota or NetworkPolicy objects exist in the cluster.

Every other workload in social-network was installed by helm at 2026-11-24T04:16:04Z and has generation 1, i.e. the pod templates of nginx-thrift, compose-post-service, text-service, the timeline, social-graph, user, mention, url-shorten, media, post-storage and unique-id services and their mongo/redis/memcached backends were never re-patched after install.

All 27 application Deployments report DESIRED 1 with AVAIL 1 / READY 1 / UPDATED 1 (custom-service reports 3 desired with no available/ready count), and all 30 application pods are Running, ready=true, restartCount 0.

All 26 application Services have ready endpoint subsets pointing at the running pods with the expected ports (e.g. nginx-thrift 10.244.234.187:8080, compose-post-service 10.244.234.134:9090, user-service 10.244.7.202:9090); no Service named custom-service exists in the namespace.

In the sampled traces of 2026-11-24T04:16:16Z to 04:16:29Z the frontend nginx-web-server returned only http.status_code=200 (10 /wrk2-api/home-timeline/read, 6 /wrk2-api/user-timeline/read, 4 /wrk2-api/post/compose spans), span_groups show error_rows 0 for every service in the sample, and the slowest span was a compose_post_server of 8.31 ms.

The only value of the label status_code on traces_span_metrics_calls_total in the window is STATUS_CODE_UNSET (no ERROR status series was returned), and the series cover the 12 services compose-post-service, home-timeline-service, media-service, nginx-web-server, post-storage-service, social-graph-service, text-service, unique-id-service, url-shorten-service, user-mention-service, user-service, user-timeline-service.

The only error lines logged in social-network during 04:10:00-04:16:30Z are startup-time MongoDB connect failures ('No suitable servers found: serverSelectionTimeoutMS expired ... ismaster on post-storage-mongodb:27017 / user-timeline-mongodb:27017 / url-shorten-mongodb:27017') from post-storage-service, user-timeline-service and url-shorten-service between 04:16:05Z and 04:16:08Z, i.e. before their mongod pods were listening; compose-post-service logged only 'Starting the compose-post-service server'.

A load generator logged wrk2 rounds against http://10.96.118.119:8080/wrk2-api/post/compose at 2026-11-24T04:16:12Z and 04:16:23Z (round #0 result: 1024 requests in 10.00s, 102.38 requests/sec), yet at query time there is no Job object anywhere in the cluster (0 items) and no pod labelled app=wrk2-job.

Root cause mechanism: the kubectl-patch applied to Deployment custom-service at 04:16:13Z inserted init container hang-init (/bin/sh -c 'sleep infinity') into the pod template; because the Deployment rolls with maxSurge 0%/maxUnavailable 100%, the healthy custom-service-5c68f797 ReplicaSet was scaled to 0 before any new pod could pass the init container, so custom-service currently has zero running application containers and 3/3 unavailable replicas.

If custom-service is expected to answer HTTP on containerPort 8080 (python3 -m http.server 8080), it is fully down: its main container has never started and no pod is Ready, so nothing serves that workload, even though no Service or Ingress exposes it and no caller of it was observed.

The social-network request path shows no failure evidence in what could be sampled: the frontend spans were all HTTP 200 with millisecond latency, every application pod is Ready with 0 restarts, and every Service has populated endpoints — so no application service is shown to be broken by this fault.

Resource shortage, quota or scheduling failure as the reason the custom-service pods are Pending is rejected: each pod has a Normal Scheduled event on sregym-worker/worker2/worker3, there are no FailedScheduling events for them, and no ResourceQuota objects exist in the cluster; the pods are Pending solely because their init container never completes.

An application-service misconfiguration or crash was considered as the fault and found unsupported: no app Deployment was patched after its helm install, all app pods have 0 restarts and no terminated/previous container state, and the only runtime error lines are the transient MongoDB-not-yet-listening messages at 04:16:05-08Z before the mongod pods accepted connections.

Recommended fix for custom-service: remove the hang-init init container (or replace 'sleep infinity' with a real completion) from Deployment custom-service in social-network, and use a rolling strategy with maxUnavailable < 100% so the previous ReplicaSet keeps serving until new pods pass their init containers.

gaps: Prometheus held only a single sample for the whole authorized window (count(up)=93 at 2026-11-24T04:16:30Z and one point per query), so no error-rate or latency trend before 04:16:30Z can be computed and pre-incident baselines are unknown; the application itself only started at 04:16:04Z, leaving ~26 s of monitored state.

The caller/consumer of custom-service is unknown: there is no Service or Ingress for it, no trace service named custom-service in Jaeger, and its main container never started so it produced no application logs; whether any workload or user depended on it cannot be verified.

Who or what issued the kubectl-patch/kubectl-rollout on Deployment custom-service at 04:16:13Z is not visible beyond the managedFields manager names and timestamps (no change-history integration is available in this Run).

A load generator (pod wrk2-job-rfc9t) logged wrk2 rounds at 04:16:12-04:16:23Z but no Job object and no pod labelled app=wrk2-job exists now; its later state and whether load generation continued is unknown, so its wrk2 latency summary (which printed -nan/0.00us percentiles) cannot be interpreted.

Trace coverage is a 1% probabilistic sample (jaeger-config.json param 0.01) and the trace view is a biased sample, so absence of error spans for a service is not proof that it served no failing requests.

A single Warning event (FailedMount 'failed to sync configmap cache: timed out waiting for the condition' on home-timeline-service at 04:16:05Z) was observed at startup; the pod is now Running and Ready, but its effect at that instant is unknown.
next_steps: Verify with the owning team whether Deployment custom-service in namespace social-network is expected to run (python3 -m http.server 8080) and remove the hang-init init container; re-check kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{namespace="social-network",deployment="custom-service"} after the fix.
Ask the change-management owner which actor applied the kubectl patch to custom-service at 2026-11-24T04:16:13Z, since change_history is not integrated in this Run.

Continue watching nginx-web-server trace latency/error signals and the wrk2 load generator once more than one Prometheus scrape exists, to confirm whether the custom-service outage has any effect on the social-network request path.
